I build things to see how they work underneath. Right now that means mechanistic interpretability of small language models: reading a transformer's residual stream with the model's own weights, and watching how it keeps, revises and reuses what it has read.

I also run my own infrastructure. This page is served from a hardened NixOS workstation at home that runs a Bitcoin node, a Lightning node and the Nostr relay this page is assembled from — every block you are reading is a signed event on that relay.

Computer Science (software engineering specialist) at the University of Toronto Scarborough. Before the language models: security, browsers, and a long trail of one-page experiments — the [directory](/directory.html) has all of them.

September 2026. Studying how transformers remember: a zero-parameter dictionary built from a model's own write directions, continuation lenses that run the model's remaining blocks on an intermediate state, and the attention heads that carry a revised fact to the output. The demos above are the plain-English version of that work.

Keeping the box alive: channels, backups, and the relay behind this page.

tags: How this page works — a block of ronishbhatt.com
drafts.content:
There is no CMS and no build step. This HTML is an empty shell with a few hundred lines of JavaScript and four self-hosted libraries ([nostr-tools](https://github.com/nbd-wtf/nostr-tools), [preact](https://preactjs.com) + [htm](https://github.com/developit/htm), [marked](https://marked.js.org), [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify)). Everything else — the header, this text, the project cards, the theme — is a Nostr event signed by this site's key.

Your browser asks [my relay](https://relay.ronishbhatt.com) first and three public relays as backups, verifies every signature, keeps the newest version of each block, and stays subscribed: when I edit something, every open tab updates. A signed snapshot is baked into the HTML for the first paint and for the day all four relays are down.

The blocks are ordinary long-form notes (kind 30023), so they open in any Nostr client — the ⌁ next to each heading is the same event on njump. The chat is NIP-17: your browser mints a key, wraps the message to mine, and my relay stores it. Unlocking with the site key turns this page into its own editor and opens the console for the box that serves it.

tags: Plant a Thought — a block of ronishbhatt.com
A real 7-million-parameter language model running in your browser. Plant a phrase into its memory, watch it surface in what it writes, then erase it.
drafts.content: The whole model is inlined, so the page is 9.5 MB. A word-level GPT trained on TinyStories; the engine is hand-written JavaScript with a KV cache — planting splices a phrase's keys and values into it, erasing compacts them out.
